defaults.gradientPolicy: none-unless-data-or-light-phenomenon; named gradients in `gradients` are allowed for title/section grounds, light phenomena and SEQUENTIAL data ramps — never on data marks, never under body text without a scrim

palettes.name: Berry Wine / Orchid Mist
palettes.wheel: single rose-wine hue, value-stepped; olive counterweight in data

palettes.name: Sage Leaf / Buttercream
palettes.wheel: yellow → yellow-green neighbours; brick red as the single far accent

palettes.name: Arctic Sky / Mulberry Wine
palettes.wheel: ice blue ↔ mulberry red-violet, both desaturated toward pastel

palettes.name: Midnight Navy / Burnt Tangerine
palettes.wheel: navy blue ↔ orange — the classic warm/cool axis at full commitment
palettes.cvd: Blue/orange axis is the safest complementary pair for deuteranopia and protanopia; keep data4 (periwinkle) and data6 (leaf) apart in adjacent series.

palettes.name: Oat Milk / Cocoa Bean
palettes.wheel: yellow-cream → brown neighbours; sage and steel as measured counterpoints

palettes.name: Graphite / Ember Copper
palettes.wheel: cool graphite blue-grey ↔ ember copper-orange
palettes.cvd: Teal/copper diverging axis survives deuteranopia via lightness spread; avoid pairing data4 (coral) with data6 (olive) in adjacent series.

palettes.name: Porcelain / Measured Indigo
palettes.wheel: single indigo hue on warm porcelain neutrals; earth counter in data

palettes.name: Obsidian / Champagne Gold
palettes.wheel: warm champagne gold ↔ cool steel blue, both restrained on obsidian
palettes.cvd: Gold/blue is deuteranopia-safe. data3 (mint) and data5 (pale gold) sit close in lightness — separate them with markers or dashing, not hue alone.

palettes.name: Slate Pine / Verdigris
palettes.wheel: green → teal neighbours; ochre and cobalt as far data counterweights
palettes.cvd: Accent verdigris vs data4 leaf-green are close for deuteranopia — never adjacent series; ochre/cobalt diverging axis is safe.

palettes.name: Ultraviolet / Chartreuse Signal
palettes.wheel: deep violet ↔ yellow-green; maximum hue distance, chroma held on one side
palettes.cvd: Violet/chartreuse reads as blue/yellow for both deuteranopia and protanopia — a safe axis. Keep chartreuse the ONLY high-chroma element per slide.

palettes.name: Cerulean / Vermilion Field
palettes.wheel: cerulean blue ↔ vermilion red-orange on warm paper — editorial daylight
palettes.cvd: Blue/vermilion diverging axis is CVD-safe; olive (data3) and ochre (data6) collide under deuteranopia — never adjacent.

palettes.name: Prussian Depth / Amber Beacon
palettes.wheel: prussian blue base; amber and rose flank its complement instead of hitting it
palettes.cvd: Amber/sky axis is safe. Rose (data3) vs mint (data4) is a red/green pair — separate by lightness and never encode a critical distinction with only these two.

palettes.name: Magma / Basalt Field
palettes.wheel: red → orange → gold neighbours on volcanic near-black; one cool outlier for charts
palettes.cvd: An analogous warm ramp reads as ONE hue family under deuteranopia — lightness steps carry the order, which is exactly why the sequential ramp works. Use data4 (violet) or data5 (jade) whenever two warm series must be told apart.

palettes.name: Polar Night / Aurora Green
palettes.wheel: green → teal → violet neighbours, the actual aurora emission sequence
palettes.cvd: Green accent vs teal data2 merge under deuteranopia — the lightness gap (L* ≈ 20) carries them; verify in grayscale. Violet/green diverging axis is safer than red/green.

palettes.name: Heliograph Charcoal / Triad
palettes.wheel: gold / teal / coral at 120° spacing — three genuinely equal categories
palettes.cvd: Reserve the triad for exactly three categories: gold, teal, coral separate cleanly under deuteranopia because each sits at a different lightness. Do not add a fourth equal category — demote it to data4.

palettes.name: Royal Indigo / Saffron
palettes.wheel: indigo ↔ saffron yellow-orange on warm ceremonial paper
palettes.cvd: Indigo/saffron is a blue/yellow axis — safe for all common CVD types. Jade (data3) and brick (data4) must never be the only distinction between two series.

palettes.name: Ionosphere Cyan / Deep Field
palettes.wheel: single electric cyan, value-stepped on abyssal blue-black; apricot counter in data
palettes.cvd: Cyan/apricot diverging axis is CVD-safe. In a monochromatic scheme the sequential ramp is the palette's native language — prefer it over multi-hue category colors.

palettes.cvd: Sarı zemin ile yeşil mürekkep protanopide de ayrışır; data5 (zeytin) ile data1 (yeşim) komşu seride kullanılmasın.

textSafety.measuredAcross: geçişin 21 noktasında ölçüldü — en kötü nokta esas alınır
